publications.notes: Read from PDF table 'LOs konjunkturanslag' (pdftotext, layout mode). Revisions vs March in brackets in the PDF: GDP -0.3/-0.2/-0.2, LFS unemployment +0.1/+0.2/+0.2, CPI +0.1/-0.2/-0.2, policy rate +0.3/+0.5/+0.3. Investment rows (mainland gross investment -0.3/0.8/1.2; oil investment -1.0/-2.0/-3.0; public investment -1.7/3.7/3.2; housing investment -3.0/2.0/3.0 as printed) are misaligned in the text extraction and should be checked against the PDF before use. The note contains NAM shift simulations: Norges Bank's higher rate path lowers inflation only 0.1-0.2 pp but keeps unemployment at 4.5% instead of falling; a 'long oil crisis' scenario (130/120/110 USD) gives higher inflation and much higher unemployment. These are LO's forecasts produced with NAM, not forecasts published by Nymoen/Bårdsen themselves; registered unemployment, wage growth and house prices are not in the table.

model_status_2026: NAM is maintained by Nymoen and Bårdsen through Normetrics (ragnar.nymoen@normetrics.no); documentation re-issued 10 Oct 2025, 10 and 18 Mar, 8 Apr, 31 May, 2 Sep and 5 Oct 2026 (https://normetrics.no/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/NAMdocumentation.pdf, 2026 vintage ~330 endogenous variables, EViews; forecast example in the documentation has forecast origin 2025Q2/2025Q3 with 90% stochastic-simulation fan charts). The documentation refers to 'the normal published forecast horizons' and 'the published model forecast', but no NAM forecast tables are published on normetrics.no after the 2017 posts and the 2017-2019 KS/KLP reports. Forecasts are delivered to model users: LO (publishes LO/NAM forecasts in Samfunnsnotat konjunkturutsiktene, March and May 2026), NHO, KLP (pension assumptions), KS (municipal wages), Samfunnsøkonomisk Analyse (house-price reports), and Finanstilsynet (NAM-FT with a bank module, used for the baseline and stress scenarios in Finansielt utsyn / the annual bank stress test, incl. June 2026).
archive_summary: Public NAM forecast material goes back to: DN/Samfunnsøkonomenes prognosepris submissions by Bårdsen and Nymoen (NAM won the prize for 2012 forecasts, DN 'Norges beste spåmenn'; the judge noted NAM was among the weakest the year before, i.e. 2011; the DN articles are paywalled so the submitted numbers could not be read; no evidence found of NAM participation after ~2013); KLP conference lecture 'Makroøkonomiske prognoser 2013-2016' (2012); Finansdepartementet seminars 2015 ('Om store prognosefeil') and January 2016 ('NAM-prognoser januar 2016'), no files; normetrics.no posts May-June 2017 (mainland GDP, registered unemployment, house prices with fan charts); Normetrics reports 1/2017-2/2019 (municipal wages 2017-2023, pension assumptions to 2035). After 2019/2020 the only public traces are the Dec 2025 policy-rate fan chart image and the LO/SØA/Finanstilsynet publications that use NAM. Track record: no systematic table of NAM forecasts next to realised outcomes is published. Evaluation material consists of Bårdsen, Kolsrud and Nymoen (2017, Journal of Forecasting, doi 10.1002/for.2459; summarised at https://normetrics.no/nam/nam-and-forecast-robustness-in-macroeconometric-models/ with a figure of NAM forecasts vs actuals 2007Q1-2011Q4: interest-rate forecasts failed after the financial crisis, others 'not so bad'), Bårdsen, Jansen and Nymoen (2002) on inflation forecast uncertainty, Falch and Nymoen (2011) on forecast accuracy of a forecast-targeting central bank, and the 2012 prognosepris. The 2021 forecast-evaluation images on normetrics.no concern CovidMod (Covid-19), not NAM. Norges Bank Watch: no edition authored by Nymoen or Bårdsen was found (only Bårdsen and Nymoen's Norges Bank Working Paper 2/2002 'Rente og inflasjon').
